questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. **

To lead by the nose

options.text: To hit someone on the nose

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e. 'To completely control someone'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• As the given idiom means* to force someone to go somewhere (with you); to lead someone by coercion. (किसी को कहीं जाने के लिए मजबूर करना (आपके साथ); जबरदस्ती किसी का नेतृत्व करना।)*
 
• E.g :- John had to lead Tom by the nose to get him to the opera.

questions.question:

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in the blank.

Akbar had a ______ reign than Babar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 2) i.e. 'longer'. **

 
• If we are comparing two entities, we use the comparative form of Adjective
 
• The comparative form of Adjective generally takes 'er' form with 'Regular adjectives. 
 
• E.g:- Gaurav is taller than his cousin.
 
• Hence, the given sentence will be: *Akbar had a** longer** reign than Babar.*

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 2) i.e. 'Explanation' **

 
• The correct spellings of the given words are:-
 
• Submission:- the action of accepting or yielding to a superior force or to the will or authority of another person.
 
• Conquer:- overcome and take control of (a place or people) by military force.
 
• Confidence:- the feeling or belief that one can have faith in or rely on someone or something.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in the blank.

She returned the book after she ______ it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. 'had read'.**

 
• *Past perfect tense* is used *when out of two actions, it is necessary to emphasize that the preceding action was completely finished before the succeeding action started.*
 
• E.g:- I had gone to Delhi last week before my father came.
 
• Hence, the correct sentence will be: She returned the book after she **had read** it.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e. 'I reach'

Since the given sentence is 2nd conditional, the structure is given below :-

 
• if/when + subject + v₁ + object, subject + will + v₁ + object.

For example:

 If I come to Delhi, I will inform you.

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate word that can substitute the given group of words.

Person with no ﬁxed abode
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. 'Nomad'**

 
• Nomad is a member of the group that travels from place to place to find fresh pasture for its animals and has no permanent home.
 
• E.g:- The withering of their grasslands forced the nomads of the Sahara to descend into the Nile valley.
 
• **Note:** The meaning of the word 'abode' is 'a place for residence', 'a house' or 'a home'. 
 
• **Note: **There is a difference in the meanings of the words, 'Abide' and 'Abode'.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. 

Eager
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. 'Keen' **

 
• **Eager: **means *strongly wanting to do or have something; desperately desirable.*
 
• **Keen: **eager, desirous
 
• **Active: **energetic, sporty
 
• **Satisfied: **pleased, contented, 
 
• **Alert: **vigilant, aware, watchful
 
• E.g:- As eager journalists told and retold the story of their naval valor, lieutenant Hobson's celebrity grew.

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

She loved herself so more that she thought of no one else. /No error
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. 'so more that she'. **

 
• In Part B of the sentence, we are talking about the extent up to which the subject loves herself.
 
• The given sense is best conveyed by 'so much' in the 2nd part of the sentence.
 
• Hence, *'more'* will be replaced by *'much'.*

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. 'Adjourn'**

 
• The correct spellings of the other words are:-
 
• **Adjourn:- to put off, to break off, to postpone something.** 
 
• **In a sentence**: *Since the jury could not decide the final decision on the case, the court hearing was adjourned for a week.* 
 
• Proceedings:- an event or a series of activities involving a set procedure.
 
• Suspicion:- a feeling or thought that something is possible, likely, or true.
 
• Discussion:- the action or process of talking about something in order to reach a decision or to exchange ideas.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.

My car broke __off__ on my way to home.
questions.solution:
The correct **option is 1) i.e. 'down'**

Let's have a look at the meanings of the given phrasal verbs.

 
• Break off:- abruptly stop talking, become severed
 
• ***Break down:- (of a machine or motor vehicle) suddenly cease to function***
 
• Break out:- (of war, fighting, or similarly undesirable things) start suddenly
 
• *'Break on'* isn't a phrasal verb.
 
• In a sentence: ***The equipment broke down after working for an hour. ***

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

There is few to be said on both sides. /No error
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 1) i.e. 'There is few'**

 
• Also, *'Few'* means "not many or none (people or things)." It is used to say that there are not a lot of people or things, in a negative sense.
 
• We use *'little'* with uncountable nouns, in a negative sense.
 
• Since we are talking about uncountable noun i.e *'what needs to be said.'*
 
• Hence, In part A of the given sentence,*** 'little' will be used instead of 'few'.​***

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in the blank.

The passengers were afraid, but the captain ______ them that there was no danger.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2,

 
• Mumbled - say something indistinctly and quietly, making it difficult for others to hear.
 
• Assured:- tell someone something positively to dispel any doubts.
 
• Pleaded:- make an emotional appeal.
 
• Claimed:- state or assert that something is the case, typically without providing evidence or proof.

Here, the sentence is trying to convey that the caption was trying to inculcate certainty.

questions.question:
**Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.**

Some people is always talking about themselves.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3) i.e. 'is always talking' **

 
• According to the rules of Subject-Verb agreement, *the verb has to agree with the given subject of the sentence.*
 
• If* the subject is singular, the verb will also be singular and vice versa.*
 
• Since we are talking about the plural noun 'people' in the 1st part, the verb will also be plural in number.
 
• Hence,* 'are'* will replace* 'is'* in 3rd part of the given sentence.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Quarrel
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e. 'Harmony' 

Quarrel means a heated argument or disagreement, typically about a trivial issue and between people who are usually on good terms.

Harmony means 'peace', 'tranquility between'. 

The meanings of the given words are given below :-

 
• **Strife :- **angry or bitter disagreement over fundamental issues; conflict
 
• **Feud :- **a prolonged and bitter quarrel or dispute
 
• **Bias :- **inclination or prejudice for or against one person or group, especially in a way considered to be unfair
 
• **Harmony :- **the combination of simultaneously sounded musical notes to produce a pleasing effect
 
• Options 1 & 2 are distant synonyms, whereas Option 3 is not related to the word.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

• As the given idiom means forget past offences or causes of conflict and be reconciled.
 
• E.g :- I feel we should let *bygones be bygones* and move on to the more important things.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.

We must start now __whereas__ it will be too late.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e. 'Else'**

__
 
• 'Else', other than additional', also represents 'in case of', 'otherwise'. 
 
• The sentence conveys the meaning that **'We must start now otherwise it will be too late'.**
 
• Since we have used conjunction that depicts contrast, the sentence will be correctly written as: We must start now **else__** it will be too late.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in the blank.

The frightened convict ______ for mercy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e. 'pleaded'.

__
 
• Mumbled:- say something indistinctly and quietly, making it difficult for others to hear.
 
• Whispered:- speak very softly using one's breath rather than one's throat, especially for the sake of secrecy.
 
• Pleaded:- make an emotional appeal.
 
• Shouted:- utter a loud cry, typically as an expression of strong emotion.
 
• Here, the sentence is trying to convey that the convict who is afraid appealed for mercy.
 
• Thus and so, the sentence will be written correctly as: The frightened convict** pleaded**__ for mercy.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. 

Strange
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. 'Abnormal' **

 
• ***Strange*** means unusual or surprising; difficult to understand or explain; Abnormal, something usual. 
 
• E.g:- It's strange that nobody told me about this before.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1) i.e. 'Located' **

 
• The given sentence, 'The Harmandir Sahib, also known as Darbar Sahib is a Gurudwara (1)______ in the city of Amritsar' is in the passive voice of the speech. 
 
• The passive voice takes** 'is/am/are+ 3rd form of the verb'. **
 
• Hence, the correct form of the verb here placed will be 'located' 
 
• The correct sentence will be: The Harmandir Sahib, also known as Darbar Sahib **is **a Gurudwara **located** in the city of Amritsar.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2) i.e. 'is'

 
• The given sentence, 'It (2)______ an eminent pilgrimage site' is in the **present tense**. 
 
• The Speech of the sentence in the paragraph is in the **'generic'** sense. 
 
• Hence,** the correct sentence** will be: It is an eminent pilgrimage site...

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 2) i.e. 'of' **

 
• 'Of' as a preposition here is correctly used. 
 
• **'Of'** as a **preposition **conveys the idea of** 'belonging', 'ownership', 'possession'.** 
 
• In the given sentence, 'an eminent pilgrimage site (3)______ Sikhism', the site belongs to Sikhism. The sense of belonging, possessive has been carried out here. 
 
• Hence, the correct preposition used here will be 'of'.
 
• Thus and so, the correct sentence will be: It is an eminent pilgrimage **site of Sikhism**.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer here is option 4) i.e. 'called'.**

 
• 'Called' as a verb is correctly used here. 
 
• As the context refers to, a site being popular among masses or population. 
 
• The category 'pilgrimage' has been given to this place by the population. 
 
• **'Called'** as a verb is used in the sense **'something which is vastly popular among masses'.**&
;nbsp;
 
• 'Named' and 'Regarded' are used to address only a name, quality or respect. It does not talk about popularity. 
 
• In the given sentence, 'It is usually (4)______ the Golden Temple in English',** 'Golden temple popularly called by people in English'. The name is 'Harmandir Sahib'. **
 
• Hence, the correct verb here will be:** 'Called'. **

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4) i.e. 'Because'. **

 
• 'Because' is the preposition that is correctly used here. 
 
• As, the sentence '______ it is plated with gold' **calls for a reason** that 'why Harmandir Sahib is known as 'golden temple'. 
 
• Thus and so, the correct sentence will be: '**because** it is plated with gold'.
